title: SparkyFitness
name: sparkyfitness
description: Fitness tracker for food, exercise, water, sleep, fasting, mood and body measurements, with goals, long-term reports and family sharing, plus sync from phone health apps, Fitbit, Strava and more. Source: https://github.com/CodeWithCJ/SparkyFitness

env.name: SPARKYFITNESS_URL
env.label: Address you'll open it on (required)
env.description: Exactly what you'll type in the browser, port included and no slash at the end, like http://192.168.1.20:3004.

env.name: SPARKYFITNESS_ENCRYPTION_KEY
env.label: Encryption key (required)
env.description: Encrypts the API keys you save for food databases and AI. Exactly 64 hex characters, so generate it with: openssl rand -hex 32. Never change it.

env.name: SPARKYFITNESS_AUTH_SECRET
env.label: Auth secret (required)
env.description: Signs logins and encrypts two-factor secrets. Generate one with: openssl rand -base64 32. Never change it.

env.name: SPARKYFITNESS_DB_PASSWORD
env.label: Database password (required)
env.description: Generate one with: openssl rand -hex 32. Keep it the same when you redeploy, or SparkyFitness can't reach its database.

env.name: SPARKYFITNESS_ADMIN_EMAIL
env.label: Admin email
env.description: Whoever signs up with this email gets the admin panel.

env.name: SPARKYFITNESS_PORT
env.label: Host port for the web UI

note: Fill in the address, encryption key, auth secret and database password before you deploy, since the stack won't start without them. The address has to be exactly what you'll type in the browser, like http://192.168.1.20:3004: the port you're using, and no slash at the end. SparkyFitness only accepts logins from that address, so if it's wrong the page still loads but signing up or logging in fails. To fix it, change the address in the stack's environment variables and redeploy. Don't change the encryption key or auth secret once it's running: a new key can't read the API keys you've saved, and a new secret logs everyone out and locks out anyone using two-factor. Then open it and sign up. If you set an admin email, sign up with that one and you'll get the admin panel. Anyone who can reach it can sign up too, so once everyone's in, add SPARKYFITNESS_DISABLE_SIGNUP = true to the stack's environment variables and redeploy. Everything you log lives in Postgres, in the sparkyfitness-db volume, with photos in sparkyfitness-uploads and backups from the admin panel in sparkyfitness-backup. Docs: codewithcj.github.io/SparkyFitness
